Convert a SingleCellExperiment object to a Cerebro file

Source: R/convertSCEToCerebro.R
convertSCEToCerebro.Rd

One-step route from a SingleCellExperiment (SCE) object, or a file holding one, to a .crb file that createShinyApp can serve. It is the SCE counterpart of convertSeuratToCerebro: both run the same preparation (group validation and renaming, marker tables, most-expressed genes and mean expression) and then hand over to an exporter built on the same core, so every storage option and feature of the Seurat route is available here.

Usage

convertSCEToCerebro(
  sce_file,
  result_dir,
  assay = "logcounts",
  experiment_name = NULL,
  organism = "Human",
  groups = NULL,
  groups_naming = NULL,
  max_group_levels = 100,
  nUMI = "nUMI",
  nGene = "nGene",
  add_all_meta_data = TRUE,
  use_delayed_array = FALSE,
  expression_matrix_mode = c("embedded", "h5"),
  codec = c("qs2", "rds"),
  viewer_binary = c("auto", "always", "never"),
  viewer_binary_threshold = 100000L,
  verbose = TRUE,
  cell_cycle = NULL,
  main_group = NULL,
  projections = NULL,
  marker_file = NULL,
  marker_method = "Diff. Expression",
  add_most_expressed_genes = TRUE,
  most_expressed_genes = NULL,
  spatial_split_by = NULL,
  extra_features = NULL,
  .source_name = NULL
)

Arguments

sce_file

A SingleCellExperiment object, or the path to a .rds (saveRDS()) or .qs2 (qs2::qs_save()) file holding one, or to an .h5ad file (read with readH5adAsSCE; see convertH5adToCerebro). There is no SCE-specific file extension: an SCE is an ordinary R object, so it is stored with whichever of these serializers was used.

result_dir

Directory the .crb is written to (created if missing). The file is named cerebro_<basename>.crb.

assay

Name of the assay to export; default "logcounts".

experiment_name

Experiment name stored in the Cerebro object. Defaults to the file's base name, or "SingleCellExperiment" for an in-memory object.

organism

Organism label (e.g. "Human", "Mouse").

groups

Character vector of colData columns to use as grouping variables. Required; an error lists the usable columns when omitted.

groups_naming

Named list renaming grouping variables (old = "new"); default NULL.

max_group_levels

Groups with more unique values than this are excluded; default 100.

nUMI, nGene

colData columns holding transcripts and expressed genes per cell. When a column is missing it is computed from the counts assay (or from assay if there is no counts).

add_all_meta_data, use_delayed_array, expression_matrix_mode, codec, verbose

As in exportFromSCE.

viewer_binary, viewer_binary_threshold

As in exportFromSCE.

cell_cycle, main_group, projections

As in exportFromSCE.

marker_file

Optional marker gene table (.csv, .tsv, .txt, .tab).

marker_method

Label for the marker table; default "Diff. Expression".

add_most_expressed_genes

Compute the most expressed genes and mean expression per group; default TRUE.

most_expressed_genes

Optional pre-computed most-expressed-genes table(s); see convertSeuratToCerebro.

spatial_split_by

Optional colData column dividing the spatial coordinates into one section per level; see exportFromSCE.

extra_features

Alternative experiments (altExp, for example antibody counts "ADT") to add to the expression data as extra features: their names, or TRUE for all. Features are named <experiment>:<feature>. They are taken from the assay of the same name as assay when it exists, otherwise from X, counts or the first assay, so check that this is on the same scale as the genes.

.source_name

Internal. Base name used for the output file and the default experiment name when sce_file is an object that was read from a file by a caller (see convertH5adToCerebro).

Value

The path of the written .crb, invisibly.

Details

Immune repertoire and HLA typing stored in metadata(sce) are exported like their @misc counterparts on a Seurat object. Attaching BCR/TCR files (bcr_file/tcr_file) is not available for SCE yet.

See also

exportFromSCE, convertSeuratToCerebro

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
convertSCEToCerebro(
  sce_file = system.file("extdata/examples/pbmc_SCE.rds",
    package = "CerebroNexus"),
  result_dir = "output",
  experiment_name = "PBMC (SCE)",
  organism = "Human",
  groups = c("sample", "cluster")
)
} # }
